manifest.name: dsh-hide-account-models
manifest.description: Hides the signed-in DeepSeek account model group in DeepSeek Harness and routes saved account selections to the official API-key provider.
manifest.author: nanwu98

bundle.text:
# dsh-hide-account-models bundle patch.
#
# One Host row, no client half, no config. The plugin filters the in-process
# `llm` provider registry and rewrites account-route selections at dispatch, so
# there is no second switch or stored state to keep in sync with the plugin
# manager. Enable or disable it from Plugins like any other bundle.

- insert:
    - id: hide-account-models
      name: 'dsh-hide-account-models'

readme.text:
A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) bundle that
hides the signed-in DeepSeek account model group from the model picker and keeps
every dispatch on the official API-key provider.

| In the picker | After enabling |
| --- | --- |
| DeepSeek account models (signed-in quota) | hidden |
| `deepseek-official` models (API key) | kept, and the only selectable group |

The plugin has no settings page and no client half. Turn it on or off from
**Plugins**, exactly like any other bundle.

Signing in to the desktop app adds a `deepseek-account` provider next to the
`deepseek-official` API-key provider. Both appear in the composer menu. If a
conversation keeps an account model selected, its next request can spend on the
account even when you intended to use your API key.

This bundle removes the account group from the catalog the picker is built from,
and rewrites an already-saved account selection to `deepseek-official` before the
request leaves the Host.

- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0` (declared in `engines.dsh`).
- An **official API key configured** under **Settings → Models** (`deepseek-official`).
  Without it there is no model left to select after the account group is hidden.
  Configure the key first, then enable this plugin.
- Any operating system. The plugin is platform-neutral.

Replace `desktop` with the profile you actually start. GitHub installs need Git
on the machine, because DSH asks the repository before downloading.

readme.section: From GitHub (recommended, pinned to a tag)
From the Release tarball (no Git needed)

readme.text:
Open **Plugins → Add plugin**, paste the repository address or the tarball URL,
and restart DSH if the page asks. Installing by bare package name only works for
a package published to npm; this bundle is currently distributed from GitHub.

After a restart, `deepseek-account` is gone from the model menu. Nothing else
changes: no new page, no new toolbar item.

1. **The catalog.** Both browser model surfaces build their catalog from
   `ctx.llm.listProviders()`. The plugin wraps that method and drops the
   `deepseek-account` entry, so the account group disappears from the menu, the
   search index, and keyboard navigation at the same time.
2. **Prepared calls.** A conversation that already saved an account model would
   still have it in the Host's per-session selection cache. The plugin wraps
   `llm.prepareCall()` (the Agent loop and title generation) and rewrites only
   `provider: "deepseek-account"` to `deepseek-official`. Every other field,
   including the model id, is preserved.
3. **Direct streams.** Some callers dispatch through `llm.stream()` without
   preparing first — the default compaction summarizer is one. The same
   provider rewrite is applied there.

The plugin intentionally does not listen to `agent/request`: that hook is
deprecated in DSH 0.2.x, and the Agent loop rejects a provider or model change
there before dispatch. Rewriting at `prepareCall`/`stream` is the supported
place to keep the route on the API key.

Disabling or removing the plugin restores the original methods and announces the
change, so the account group comes back immediately without a restart.

- **Configure `deepseek-official` first.** The plugin does not check whether the
  official route has a usable key. If it does not, the picker will be empty and
  requests will fail with the official route's error instead of spending on the
  account. That failure is intentional; it is safer than a silent fallback.
- **Old conversations.** A session saved with an account model shows the
  "select a model" prompt until you choose an official model. If you send before
  choosing, the request is prepared against `deepseek-official` with the same
  model id.
- **Model ids are not translated.** If the account catalog and the official
  catalog name a model differently, a rewritten request can be rejected by the
  provider. Pick an official model in that conversation once and the problem
  does not come back.
- **Nothing is rewritten on disk.** Session logs keep their history; only the
  outgoing request is rerouted.

The plugin is a pure in-process filter:

- **No network requests.** It never contacts DeepSeek or any other host.
- **No files.** It does not read or write configuration, credentials, logs, or
  session data.
- **No telemetry.** It reports nothing anywhere.
- **No credential access.** It only calls the `llm` service that DSH already
  mounted; it never resolves, reads, or copies an API key or account token.

It reads provider metadata (`id`, `name`) from the `llm` service and writes only
one thing: the in-memory provider list that the UI reads.

Turn the bundle off with its switch in **Plugins**; the account group returns at
once. Remove it entirely with:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-hide-account-models
```

Removing the plugin does the same; it has no state to clean up.

- DSH `0.2.2-rc.1` through `0.2.x`. The bundle relies on the provider ids
  `deepseek-account` / `deepseek-official` and on `ctx.llm.listProviders()` and
  `ctx.llm.prepareCall()` from that release line.
- A future DSH release that renames those providers or stops projecting the
  provider list into the catalog will make the filter a no-op. Disable the
  bundle if the picker misbehaves rather than leaving it installed.
- This is a community plugin, not an official DeepSeek project.

Pure ESM JavaScript, zero dependencies, no build step. Run the unit tests:

```sh
npm test
```

The tests use a fake `llm` service and a fake Cordis context. They cover the
provider filter, the `prepareCall` and `stream` rewrites, restoration of the
prototype methods through a traceable proxy, and coexistence with another plugin
that patches the same method later.

The repository also publishes a format-1 market index for **Plugins → Discover →
Index sources**:

- jsDelivr (recommended):
  `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/nanwu98/dsh-hide-account-models@main/index.json`
- GitHub raw:
  `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nanwu98/dsh-hide-account-models/main/index.json`

The plugin is not affiliated with DeepSeek. It manipulates the harness's
in-process provider registry; review the source before enabling it in a
profile you depend on.
